fixes.explanation: That's it: "Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled." Jesus promises that they will be filled. That's His word to people who hunger and thirst for what's right. I wish every batch I pulled out of the oven came with a promise like that.
Yes, baker! "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God." That's a big name to be handed. Jesus gives it to the people who make peace. They're the group He names.
The scribes don't show up in these verses. The group Jesus names is the peacemakers. He says, "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God." That's the name they're given.

That's it, baker. "Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness…" Jesus says they're persecuted for doing right, not for doing wrong. And He still calls them blessed. That's the kind of suffering He's talking about.
Foolishness is a fun guess, friend. But Jesus' word is righteousness. "Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness…" He's talking about suffering for doing right.

Hiding is a natural thought when people are insulting you, friend. But Jesus doesn't say that here. He says, "Rejoice and be glad…" That's His word to those who are insulted and persecuted because of Him.
Yes! "Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven…" The reward is great, and Jesus puts it in heaven. He gives them that to rejoice about.
It's an understandable guess, friend. But in this verse Jesus puts their reward in heaven. He says, "…great is your reward in heaven…" That's where He says it is.
The temple is a fair guess, friend. But Jesus doesn't mention it here. He says, "…great is your reward in heaven…" That's the place He names.

Nice idea, but Jesus doesn't mention it. He asks, "…how can it be made salty again?" Then He says it is "…no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by men." That's where the salt ends up.

Sun-drying sounds like a thing a person would try, but it isn't in this verse. Jesus says the salt that loses its savor is "…no longer good for anything, except to be thrown out and trampled by men." That's the only ending He gives it. Nothing about the sun.
Right, there are no loopholes here. Jesus says, "A city on a hill cannot be hidden." It's a plain statement. Trying harder doesn't change it.

That's where it goes. People "…set it on a stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house." A lit lamp gets put up where it can do its job. That's what Jesus says people do instead of putting it under a basket.

Under a bed is a creative hiding spot, I'll give you that. But Jesus says people don't hide a lit lamp. Instead, "…they set it on a stand, and it gives light to everyone in the house." The basket is the only hiding place He mentions.
I'd love for people to notice my apron, I'll admit it. But Jesus' word is deeds. "…that they may see your good deeds and glorify your Father in heaven." That's what He says people will see.
A good fortune would be nice, friend. But Jesus says people will see their good deeds. That's the word in verse 16. It's about what they do.
